title: Wire the references
intro: An array of objects holds references, not objects: each box is an arrow to an object that lives somewhere else. Run the code by wiring every box to its object.

rounds.prompt: Run the code: click a box of `{name}`, then the object the code puts in it.
rounds.right: Every box now holds an arrow. Each one is a copy of the arrow in a variable: two references, one object.

why.wrong: `{name}[{box}] = {expected};` copies the arrow in `{expected}`, so box {box} points at the object `{expected}` points at, not at `{chosen}`'s.
why.unassigned: No line writes to `{name}[{box}]`, so it keeps its default and points at nothing.

rounds.right: Follow the arrow out of `{name}[{box}]`: it reaches the object whose name is `"{who}"`, and that's what `getName()` returns.

why.getName: Follow the arrow out of `{name}[{box}]`: `getName()` runs on whichever object the arrow reaches.

rounds.prompt: A new array, and only two lines this time. Wire them up.
rounds.right: A box for references starts as `null`: no arrow, no object. `new Planet[3]` made three boxes and not a single Planet.

why.wrong: `{name}[{box}] = {expected};` copies the arrow in `{expected}`, so box {box} points at the object `{expected}` points at, not at `{chosen}`'s.
why.unassigned: No line writes to `{name}[{box}]`, so it keeps its default and points at nothing.
why.empty: `""` would be a String object, and this box is for `Planet` references. Nothing was put in it, so it holds the default for a reference: no arrow at all.
why.zero: `0` is the default for number boxes. This box holds a reference to a `Planet`, and a reference starts out pointing at nothing.
why.object: `new Planet[3]` builds three boxes and no Planet objects: an object only exists once `new Planet(…)` runs. This box points at nothing.

rounds.right: There is no object at the end of a `null` reference, so there is nothing to call `getName()` on: Java stops with a `NullPointerException`.

why.null: `getName()` can only run on an object, and `null` is no object: there is no `name` to hand back, not even a missing one.
why.empty: There's no `Planet` at the end of a `null` reference, so there is no `name` to return, not even an empty one.
